tagline: Over the hills of Holmes County, at a buggy's pace.
intro: The byway makes a double loop through Holmes County on SR 39, US 62 and the back roads between, from Loudonville on the Mohican River through Millersburg, Berlin and Walnut Creek and over to Sugarcreek. It winds, and it goes up and down a good deal.

Half the county is Amish, the highest share of any county in the country. A horse and buggy covers perhaps 10 to 35 miles in a day, so the stores, banks and doctors have stayed within reach. The settlement dates from 1808, and Jonas Stutzman built his cabin on Walnut Creek the year after.

moments.title: Behalt, Berlin
moments.text: An Amish blacksmith wished for a place where tourists could learn why the Plain people live as they do. Heinz Gaugel answered with a 265-foot painting, fourteen years in the making.

moments.title: Guggisberg Cheese, Charm
moments.text: Baby Swiss cheese was worked out here in the mid-1960s. Where the hamlet of Charm got its name, nobody can say for sure.

moments.title: Mount Hope
moments.text: A community of 197 on State Route 241 with a weekly auction of livestock and household goods. Close by, Horse Progress Days is given over to horse-powered machines.
